Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the unified private/hosted options. We have one sticking point from procurement: the current pilot commitment and SKU mix in SOW_v2 pushes our effective price above the budgeted bar for Q4.

I've attached the SOW (HealthSpark_SOW_v2.pdf) and our internal target numbers. Can you advise on whether Redwood can accommodate either option and what approvals you need?

Sofia — reviewed the SOW and ran scenarios. Quick notes: 

- Option A (onboarding credit): a one-time credit equal to ~2 weeks of expected token spend would get them through pilot initiation but provides limited behavioral guarantees.
- Option B (3-month blended rate): offering a 12% blended discount months 1–3 against the MRR in the SOW will likely win the deal but reduces gross margin materially (see worksheet).
- Margin protection clause: we can accept a clause that prevents retroactive rate increases during the pilot, but it must be explicitly time-boxed and tied to minimum usage thresholds.

I've attached a short finance impact worksheet with projected margin at 0%, 12%, and 15% concession levels (finance-impact-worksheet.xlsx). My recommendation: approve Option B at a max 12% concession with the following guardrails: 1) minimum 3-month commit of stated usage; 2) cap on total onboarding credits; 3) auto-revert to standard rates after month 3 with observed usage reconciliation.

If this is escalated beyond 12%, we need VP/CFO authorization and a one-off allowance in our discount ledger.

—Marissa
